newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen jumping after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen jumping after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to bolt higher with bonds on Friday after the September jobs data came in much softer than expected, analysts said.
"This is far weaker than expected. We could get to a Dow 6,000 right here," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at VALUE Line Asset Management in New York.

The U.S. long bond jumped 1-9/32, knocking its yield down to 6.73 percent after the news. The December S&P 500 index futures contract climbed 3.60 to 701.30, indicating the Dow may open up about 28 points.

It's very clear the economy slowed in September. It's obviously very good news for the Federal Reserve and for the bond market but a mixed blessing for stocks because it will intensify worries about earnings. The shift to the defensive side of the market will only increase," commented Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
